ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

3. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

4. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

5. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

11. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 13.4.1 Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
